---
title: Performance design
description: The data structures behind the benchmarks — the verified path index, inline path storage, memchr line scans and the rebuilt-on-load wire format.
type: explanation
---

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Sourcier's performance comes from a small set of data-structure decisions,
each of which trades complexity in one place for a constant-factor win where
tools spend their time. This page walks through those decisions and the
numbers they produce. All measurements come from the bundled criterion suite
(`cargo bench -p sourcier-core`) on the reference machine, comparing 2.0
against the 1.0 baseline in the same measurement window; treat the numbers
as indicative.

## A verified open-addressed path index

Path lookups run through a per-map open-addressed index from path hash to
entry. Three properties define it:

- **Seeded per map.** The hash uses two parallel multiply chains and one
  combine multiply with a seed that differs per map, so adversarial
  collision patterns cannot be precomputed (HashDoS resistance).
- **Verified probes.** A hash match is only a prefilter: every probe is
  verified against the stored path bytes. Collisions can never produce a
  wrong answer, whatever the hash quality.
- **Dense and predictable.** Linear probing at a load factor of 0.5 with 4
  bytes per slot; probes terminate on the first empty slot, so misses are as
  cheap as hits.

The measured trade-off: 2.0 spends about 20% more latency on hits
(~41 us vs ~34 us per 2,000 lookups) in exchange for byte-exact
verification, zero allocations at finalization and roughly half the
lookup-state memory. Misses, at ~33 us per 2,000, are a new tracked
scenario.

## Inline path storage

Entries store paths with short-string optimization: paths up to 30 bytes
live inline inside the 32-byte payload, and longer paths fall back to a
`Box<str>`. Most source-tree paths fit the inline bound, which keeps the hot
lookup path at two dependent cache lines — the index slot and the entry —
and makes finalization allocation-free for typical trees.

## One sort, one pass

Finalization is a single unstable sort with a registration-order tiebreak
plus one O(n) pass that assigns ids and builds the index. File contents are
never copied during finalization. The measured effect:

| Scenario | 1.0 | 2.0 | Change |
| -------- | --- | --- | ------ |
| Finalize 100 files × 50 lines | ~64 us | ~41 us | **-35%** |
| Finalize 500 files × 100 lines | ~709 us | ~513 us | **-28%** |
| Finalize phase only, 2,000 × 200 lines | ~3.7 ms | ~2.8 ms | **-25%** |

## memchr line scans

The `view` feature indexes every file's line boundaries with a single
`memchr`-accelerated scan — the 1.0 counting pre-pass is gone — and stores 4
bytes per line as `u32` offsets, which caps indexable files at 4 GiB. Line
and column navigation is binary search over that compact list:

| Scenario | 1.0 | 2.0 | Change |
| -------- | --- | --- | ------ |
| 1,000 multi-line `view` extractions | ~14.4 us | ~4.4 us | **-70%** |
| Line offsets for 100 files × 1,000 lines | ~0.79 ms | ~0.69 ms | **-12%** |
| 1,000 offset-to-(line, col) probes | — | ~8.2 us | new |
| Single-line `view_str` span | — | ~257 ns | new |

Per-file line offsets live in a dense `Vec<Option<LineOffsets>>` indexed by
id, so the view hot path performs no hashing at all. The opt-in `parallel`
feature spreads the scan across cores with `rayon`; on the 2-core reference
VM the thread-pool overhead outweighed the scan savings, which is why it is
not a default.

<Aside type="note">
	The `builder/*`, `position_from_offset/*` and `offset_from_position/*`
	benchmark tracks pin the cost of the 2.0 additions; the original
	`finalize`, `get_id`, `view` and `line_offsets` tracks are unchanged.
</Aside>

## The wire format carries data, not derived state

Serialized payloads contain only the raw entries and the phase flag. The
redundant `path_to_id` table of the 1.0 format is gone: the index is derived
from the sorted entries and rebuilt on load, and 1.0 payloads still
deserialize with the redundant field ignored. The entry hash and sequence
number are likewise derived state — the hash depends on the per-map seed —
so they are rebuilt rather than persisted.

The DX additions delegate to the same machinery rather than adding new
paths: the builder is an inline newtype over the map, the offset bridge
reuses the per-file `LineOffsets` index, and `PositionDisplay` renders
lazily from borrowed data. `rt-feedback` uses atomics only; no locks are
taken on the reporting path.

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Tuning performance" href="/guides/tuning-performance/" /> to apply these characteristics in your build.
- Read <LinkCard title="The two-phase lifecycle" href="/explanation/two-phase-lifecycle/" /> for the phase boundary that makes the index possible.
- Check <LinkCard title="Position encoding" href="/reference/position-encoding/" /> for the packed layouts behind the numbers.

---
title: Safety and stability
description: How Sourcier forbids unsafe code, seals its traits, keeps error enums non_exhaustive, and pins behavior with a layered test suite.
type: explanation
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Sourcier makes promises that tools can build on: no unsafe code, a stable
and semver-checked API, and behavior pinned by property, snapshot and
coverage-verified tests. This page explains each guarantee and how it is
enforced.

## No unsafe code

The whole workspace carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Every guarantee in
the crate — bit packing, index probing, zero-copy views — is expressed in
safe Rust. There is no unsafe block to audit, and the compiler rejects any
introduction of one.

## Sealed traits and non_exhaustive errors

Two type-level decisions keep future releases from breaking your code:

- **The `FileId` trait is sealed.** Its only implementations are `u8` and
  `u16`, and the sealing module makes downstream implementations
  impossible. New methods with default implementations can therefore be
  added to the trait in a minor release without breaking any downstream
  code.
- **Error enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`.** `MapError` and `PositionError`
  can gain variants in minor releases without a semver-breaking change.
  Match arms outside the crate include a catch-all arm; the compiler
  enforces this.

## Semver policy

The public API documented on docs.rs is stable and follows semantic
versioning from 2.0.0 onward. Two specifics worth knowing:

- The packed `u64` layouts are documented so raw values can be persisted;
  they are stable across semver-compatible releases. See
  [Position encoding](/reference/position-encoding/).
- The 2.0 wire format dropped the redundant `path_to_id` table, and 1.0
  payloads that still carry the field deserialize without error — forward
  compatibility is explicit and tested.

## The layered test suite

The repository ships unit, integration, property-based, snapshot and doc
tests:

| Layer | Tool | Pins |
| ----- | ---- | ---- |
| Unit and integration | `cargo test` / `cargo nextest run` | Per-module behavior, builder and navigation flows |
| Property-based | `proptest` | Position encoding round trips, line/col to offset inverse mapping, map lookup consistency, first-registration-wins duplicate resolution at hundreds-of-files scale |
| Snapshot | `insta` | YAML snapshots of map serialization, view extraction, packed positions and error messages |
| Doc tests | `cargo test` | Every code example in the rustdoc compiles and runs |

The property suite also covers adversarial deserialized maps that exceed the
id capacity, and the 4 GiB line-offset limit is exercised end to end with
lazily committed allocations, so oversized-file paths are tested for real.

Snapshot files live in `sourcier-core/src/tests/snapshots/` and are
committed; regenerate them after an intentional change with
`INSTA_UPDATE=always cargo test`.

## Coverage and static checks

CI runs the full gate:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo test --workspace --all-features      # unit, integration, property, doc tests
cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features
cargo llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --summary-only
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
cargo deny check                           # licenses, advisories, bans, sources`} />

Coverage measured with `cargo-llvm-cov` reports 100% of functions covered;
`llvm-cov show` confirms every line and every reachable region executes. The
summary table reports 99.9% for lines and regions — the residual counts are
uncallable compiler artifacts (definition-site copies of generic code), not
missing tests.

`missing_docs` is denied workspace-wide, so every public item carries
documentation, and rustdoc builds with warnings denied.

## The MSRV contract

The minimum supported Rust version is 1.99, verified in CI with `cargo
check` across feature configurations. The crate uses Edition 2024.

## Next steps

- Read <LinkCard title="The two-phase lifecycle" href="/explanation/two-phase-lifecycle/" /> for the invariants the tests pin.
- Check <LinkCard title="Errors" href="/reference/errors/" /> for the variants the `non_exhaustive` policy applies to.
- Browse the [repository](https://github.com/elcoosp/sourcier) for the CI workflows and `deny.toml`.


---

---
title: The two-phase lifecycle
description: Why SourceFilesMap splits into a mutable build phase and an immutable lookup phase, and how the type-state builder enforces the boundary.
type: explanation
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Every `SourceFilesMap` lives through two phases: a mutable **build phase** in
which files are registered, and an immutable **lookup phase** in which ids
exist and queries run in constant time. The phase boundary is the
`finalize` call, and it is what allows both phases to be fast.

## The build phase

During the build phase the map is an append-only registry. `add_file`,
`add_files` and `add_path` append entries — path, content and registration
order — without doing any sorting, hashing or index construction. Nothing
about ids exists yet: ids are an output of finalization, not an input.

This keeps registration as cheap as possible. A tool that discovers files
while walking a directory tree, or that ingests files from a language-server
client, pays only the cost of storing each entry.

## What finalization does

`finalize` performs three steps in one pass structure:

1. **Sort.** Entries are sorted by path with a single unstable sort. Ties —
   entries that registered the same path — keep registration order.
2. **Deduplicate.** For duplicate paths, the first registration wins and
   later ones are dropped. The rule holds deterministically even at
   hundreds-of-duplicates scale, which property tests pin.
3. **Assign ids.** Files receive one-based ids in sorted path order, so the
   same set of files always produces the same ids.

Finalization is zero-allocation for typical source trees: paths up to 30
bytes live inline inside their entries, file contents are never copied, and
the lookup index is built over the already-stored paths. After the call the
map is immutable.

## The lookup phase

Immutability is the performance trick. Because the entry set cannot change
after finalization, the path index can be a verified open-addressed hash
table sized once, with no tombstones, no rehashing and no mutation
synchronization. `get_id`, `get_path`, `get_content` and `get` run in
constant time; line and column navigation runs in O(log n) over the per-file
line index.

Iterating a map before finalization yields nothing: `Iter` filters on the
phase flag because ids only exist afterwards.

<Aside type="note">
	Serialized payloads carry only the raw entries and the phase flag. The
	lookup state is rebuilt on load, so a deserialized map behaves exactly
	like a finalized one.
</Aside>

## Why the builder exists

The raw map tracks its phase at runtime and reports mistakes as errors:
`MapError::Finalized` when you mutate after finalization,
`MapError::AlreadyFinalized` when you finalize twice. Those errors are part
of the API for tools that must keep a map through both phases.

`SourceFilesBuilder` removes the mistakes at the type level. It wraps a
build-phase map and exposes only the registration API, so mutation after
finalization cannot be expressed, and its `finalize` consumes the builder
and returns a map that is already in its lookup phase:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::SourceFilesBuilder;

let files = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::new()
    .add_file("src/main.rs", b"fn main() {}")
    .expect("capacity available")
    .add_file("src/lib.rs", b"pub mod utils;")
    .expect("capacity available")
    .finalize()
    .expect("no capacity issue");`} />

The phase errors are unrepresentable through the builder; the compiler
enforces the lifecycle. Choose the builder when the lifecycle is linear —
register, finalize, then query — and the raw map when a tool legitimately
moves a single map between phases.

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Registering source files" href="/guides/registering-files/" /> for the registration recipes the build phase offers.
- Read <LinkCard title="Performance design" href="/explanation/performance-design/" /> for the verified index that finalization builds.
- Check the <LinkCard title="API surface" href="/reference/api/" /> for the exact signatures of both phases.


---

---
title: Why Sourcier exists
description: The problem of cheap diagnostics positions in compilers, linters and language servers, and the design Sourcier chose for it.
type: explanation
---

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Tools that report diagnostics — compilers, linters, formatters, language
servers and code editors — handle positions constantly. Every warning, error,
highlight, jump target and rename needs to say where it points. The obvious
representation, a `String` path plus a handful of `usize` fields per
diagnostic, is expensive in every dimension that matters at scale.

## The cost of the obvious representation

A diagnostic position that stores its file path as a `String` pays repeatedly
for that choice:

- **Memory.** A path is stored, cloned or re-allocated for every position
  that carries it. A codebase with a million diagnostics stores the same
  paths a million times, directly or behind reference counters.
- **Comparison and ordering.** Sorting diagnostics by location means
  comparing strings before comparing numbers. String comparison is slower
  than integer comparison and harder to make cache-friendly.
- **Serialization.** Every position serializes its path again. Wire payloads
  and caches bloat, and round trips can silently change path formatting.
- **Locality.** A position spread over five or more fields is not one value:
  it is five values that must travel, hash, compare and persist together.

Positions also need to resolve back to the exact bytes they cover — for
quick fixes, for snippets in reports, for hover content. That resolution
needs the file content, which compounds the problem: content lookups should
be as cheap as the positions themselves.

## The Sourcier answer

Sourcier splits the problem in two and gives each half the cheapest possible
representation:

1. **A single immutable registry holds the heavy data.** Files are registered
   once, deduplicated and sorted during finalization, and the map then
   answers path, id and content lookups in constant time. Heavy data exists
   exactly once, no matter how many positions point at it.
2. **A position is one `u64`.** File id, start line, start column, end line
   and end column are bit-packed into a single machine word. Positions are
   `Copy`, compare as integers, hash as integers, serialize as integers and
   order lexicographically by construction.

A million diagnostics therefore carry a million machine words plus one
registry — not a million copies of paths and field tuples.

<Aside type="note">
	The packed layout is documented and stable, so raw `u64` values can be
	persisted and reloaded. See
	[Position encoding](/reference/position-encoding/) for the bit tables.
</Aside>

## What Sourcier is not

Sourcier is not a source-map implementation for transpiled code: it does not
map between source and generated files, and it does not encode token names or
mappings segments. It tracks positions in the files a tool actually reads.
If your tool parses source files and reports locations inside them, Sourcier
is designed for you.

## Design values

The API follows from four commitments:

- **Cheap by default.** Positions pack with no validation cost; validation is
  an opt-in `try_new` away. Finalization performs no per-path heap
  allocation for typical source trees.
- **Correct under pressure.** The path index verifies every probe against
  the stored bytes, so adversarial keys cannot precompute collisions, and
  duplicate registrations resolve deterministically.
- **Typed at the boundaries.** The `FileId` trait is sealed, error enums are
  `#[non_exhaustive]`, and the whole workspace forbids unsafe code.
- **Bytes when you need them.** The `view` feature keeps a compact line
  index per file, so any position resolves to the exact bytes it covers.

## Next steps

- Read <LinkCard title="The two-phase lifecycle" href="/explanation/two-phase-lifecycle/" /> for the build-finalize-lookup split that makes the registry immutable.
- Read <LinkCard title="Performance design" href="/explanation/performance-design/" /> for the data structures behind the constants.
- Follow <LinkCard title="Your first source map" href="/tutorials/getting-started/" /> to see the design in ten minutes of code.

---
title: Handling errors
description: Distinguish every MapError and PositionError variant, match them exhaustively despite non_exhaustive, and recover with the right fallback.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to handle the two error enums Sourcier returns:
`MapError` for building or querying a map, and `PositionError` for checked
position constructors. Both enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so match arms
outside the crate always include a catch-all arm.

## Match MapError variants

`MapError` has five variants. This example recovers from each one
appropriately:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{MapError, SourceFilesBuilder};

fn register(builder: &mut SourceFilesBuilder<u8>, path: &str, data: &[u8]) {
    if let Err(err) = builder.add_file_mut(path, data) {
        match err {
            MapError::TooManyFiles { max } => {
                eprintln!("id type exhausted: at most {max} files");
                // Recover: switch to u16 ids, or stop accepting files.
            }
            MapError::FileTooLarge { size } => {
                eprintln!("file of {size} bytes exceeds the 4 GiB line-offset limit");
                // Recover: skip the file; views resolve to None for it.
            }
            MapError::PathNotUtf8 { path } => {
                eprintln!("skipping non-UTF-8 path: {path}");
                // Recover: skip; the path carries U+FFFD replacements.
            }
            // The map cannot be modified after finalization; with the
            // type-state builder these two variants are unrepresentable,
            // but the raw map can still report them.
            MapError::Finalized | MapError::AlreadyFinalized => {
                unreachable!("builder guarantees the build phase")
            }
            // non_exhaustive: always keep a catch-all arm.
            other => {
                eprintln!("unexpected map error: {other}");
            }
        }
    }
}`} />

The variants and when they occur:

| Variant | Fields | Occurs when |
| ------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `TooManyFiles` | `max: usize` | Registration or finalization exceeds the id type capacity (255 for `u8`, 65,535 for `u16`) |
| `AlreadyFinalized` | — | `finalize` is called on an already finalized map |
| `Finalized` | — | The finalized map is mutated (`add_file`, `add_files`, `add_path`) |
| `FileTooLarge` | `size: u64` | A file exceeds the 4 GiB `u32` line-offset limit |
| `PathNotUtf8` | `path: String` | `add_path` receives a path that is not valid UTF-8 |

<Aside type="tip">
	`SourceFilesBuilder` exposes only the registration API and `finalize`
	consumes it, so `MapError::Finalized` and `MapError::AlreadyFinalized`
	cannot be produced through the builder. They remain reachable through the
	raw `SourceFilesMap`, which keeps its phase errors at runtime.
</Aside>

## Handle checked position failures

`PositionError` has a single variant, `InvalidRange`, which carries the
rejected span:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{AbsolutePosition, PositionError};

match AbsolutePosition::<u8>::try_new(1, 2, 1, 1, 1) {
    Ok(pos) => println!("packed as {}", pos.as_raw()),
    Err(PositionError::InvalidRange { start_line, start_col, end_line, end_col }) => {
        eprintln!(
            "invalid span {start_line}:{start_col}-{end_line}:{end_col}"
        );
    }
    Err(_) => unreachable!("only one variant exists today"),
}`} />

A valid span satisfies all of the following:

- `start_line >= 1` and `end_line >= 1`
- `start_col >= 1` and `end_col >= 1`
- `start_line < end_line`, or `start_line == end_line && start_col <= end_col`

## Read the display strings

Both enums implement `std::error::Error` through `thiserror`, and their
display strings are part of the API surface and covered by snapshot tests:

<Code lang="text" code={`cannot register more than 255 files for this file id type
the source files map has already been finalized
cannot modify the source files map after finalization
file content of 4294967296 bytes exceeds the 4 GiB line offset limit
path is not valid UTF-8: caf<U+FFFD>.txt
invalid position range: start 2:1 must not come after end 1:1 and all lines and columns must be at least 1`} />

## Plan for capacity up front

`MapError::TooManyFiles` is the variant most tools meet first. Choose the id
type before registration starts: `u8` addresses 255 files, `u16` addresses
65,535. Check `remaining_capacity` on a builder to fail early with your own
message instead of surfacing the library error.

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Registering source files" href="/guides/registering-files/" /> to avoid capacity errors in the first place.
- Check the <LinkCard title="Errors reference" href="/reference/errors/" /> for the complete variant list with field tables.
- Read <LinkCard title="Safety and stability" href="/explanation/safety-and-stability/" /> to see how `non_exhaustive` interacts with the semver policy.

---
title: Installation
description: Add Sourcier to a Rust project from crates.io or Git, verify the MSRV and trim feature flags for a leaner build.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to add Sourcier to an existing Rust project and to configure
its feature flags. Sourcier supports Rust 1.99 and later (Edition 2024); the
MSRV is verified in CI across feature configurations.

## Add the dependency

<Tabs>
	<TabItem label="cargo add">
		<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo add sourcier`} />

		Cargo adds the latest `2.0` release and enables the default features.
	</TabItem>
	<TabItem label="Cargo.toml">
		<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
sourcier = "2.0"`} />
	</TabItem>
</Tabs>

You only ever depend on `sourcier`. It re-exports the full API of the
`sourcier-core` engine crate, which exists so the implementation can stay
small and the facade stable.

<Aside type="note">
	Prefer a living dependency? Track the repository directly:

	<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
sourcier = { git = "https://github.com/elcoosp/sourcier", branch = "main" }`} />
</Aside>

## Verify the install

Compile a three-line program that touches the public API:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{SourceFilesBuilder, SourceFilesMap};

let files = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::new()
    .add_file("a.rs", b"fn a() {}")
    .expect("capacity available")
    .finalize()
    .expect("no capacity issue");

let _: &str = files.get_path(1).expect("file present");`} />

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo build`} />

A successful build prints nothing. Any `unresolved import` error means the
dependency did not resolve — check that `Cargo.lock` contains `sourcier`.

## Trim feature flags

All features except `parallel` are enabled by default and forwarded to
`sourcier-core`. Disable the ones you do not need for a leaner build:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
sourcier = { version = "2.0", default-features = false, features = ["view"] }`} />

This keeps the line-offset index and byte extraction while dropping
serialization and runtime statistics. See
[Feature flags](/reference/feature-flags/) for the full matrix and what each
feature gates.

<Aside type="caution">
	Disabling `view` removes `view`, `view_str`, `position_from_offset`,
	`offset_from_position` and `display_position`. Code that calls them fails
	to compile until you re-enable the feature.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Your first source map" href="/tutorials/getting-started/" /> for the complete workflow.
- Follow <LinkCard title="Registering source files" href="/guides/registering-files/" /> to put the dependency to work.
- Check <LinkCard title="Feature flags" href="/reference/feature-flags/" /> before trimming further.


---

---
title: Views and navigation
description: Extract the exact bytes of a span, bridge byte offsets and packed positions, and render path:line:column diagnostics without allocating.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to turn positions back into source bytes and to navigate files
byte-accurately. Everything on this page requires the default `view` feature.

## Extract the bytes of a span

`view` returns the exact bytes a position covers, including multi-line spans
and the line terminators inside them:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{AbsolutePosition, SourceFilePosition, SourceFilesMap};

let mut files = SourceFilesMap::<u8>::new();
files
    .add_file("src/main.rs", b"fn main() {\\n    println!(\\"Hello\\");\\n}")
    .expect("capacity available");
files.finalize().expect("no capacity issue");

let id = files.get_id("src/main.rs").expect("file present");
let pos = AbsolutePosition::new(id, 2, 5, 2, 22);

assert_eq!(files.view(id, &pos), Some(&b"println!(\\"Hello\\");"[..]));`} />

For UTF-8 source, `view_str` returns a `&str` instead and yields `None` when
the span would cut a multi-byte character:

<Code lang="rust" code={`let text = files.view_str(id, &pos).expect("utf-8 span");
assert_eq!(text, "println!(\\"Hello\\");");`} />

`view` also handles zero-width spans, which resolve to the empty slice at the
requested point.

## Convert byte offsets to positions and back

The map bridges between byte offsets and packed positions in O(log n) over
the per-file line index, with no allocation:

<Code lang="rust" code={`let pos = files.position_from_offset(id, 4).expect("in range");
assert_eq!(pos.start_line(), 2);
assert_eq!(pos.start_column(), 1);

assert_eq!(files.offset_from_position(id, &pos), Some(4));`} />

`position_from_offset` returns a zero-width point position. Offsets up to and
including the content length resolve: the content length maps to the column
one past the last byte, the conventional insertion anchor at the end of the
file.

<Aside type="caution">
	Offsets whose line or column cannot be represented by the packed encoding
	resolve to `None`: files of more than 65,535 lines, or lines longer than
	255 bytes.
</Aside>

## Render diagnostics

`display_position` renders `path:line:column` through a borrowed
`PositionDisplay`. Building it performs no allocation, so it is cheap to
format diagnostics at high volume:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{SourceFilesBuilder, SourceFilePosition};

let files = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::new()
    .add_file("src/main.rs", b"fn main() {}")
    .expect("capacity available")
    .finalize()
    .expect("no capacity issue");

let id = files.get_id("src/main.rs").expect("file present");
let pos = files.position_from_offset(id, 4).expect("in range");

let rendered = files.display_position(id, &pos).expect("present").to_string();
assert_eq!(rendered, "src/main.rs:1:5");`} />

## Work with the line index directly

`line_offsets` exposes the per-file `LineOffsets` index that backs the
operations above. You can also compute one standalone from any bytes:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::LineOffsets;

let offsets = LineOffsets::compute(b"one\\ntwo").expect("within 4 GiB limit");
assert_eq!(offsets.line_count(), 2);

// Byte range of line 2 (one-based; line 0 resolves to nothing).
assert_eq!(offsets.line_range(2), Some(4..7));

// Offset to (line, column), both one-based.
assert_eq!(offsets.line_col_from_offset(5), Some((2, 2)));

// (line, column) back to offset.
assert_eq!(offsets.offset_from_line_col(2, 1), Some(4));`} />

Other accessors: `content_length` returns the total byte length, and
`line_starts` exposes the compact `u32` offset list.

## Know the limits

| Limit | Value | Behavior when exceeded |
| ----- | ----- | ---------------------- |
| File size for the line index | 4 GiB (`u32` offsets) | `LineOffsets::compute` fails with `MapError::FileTooLarge`; files registered through a map resolve no views |
| Lines per file | 65,535 (`u16`) | Offset conversion returns `None` |
| Columns per line | 255 byte columns (`u8`) | Offset conversion returns `None` |

Line offsets use a single `memchr`-accelerated scan and store 4 bytes per
line. Enable the opt-in `parallel` feature to spread the scan across cores —
see [Tuning performance](/guides/tuning-performance/).

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Sharing usage statistics" href="/guides/usage-statistics/" /> to observe finalization activity across maps.
- Follow <LinkCard title="Tuning performance" href="/guides/tuning-performance/" /> for large file sets.
- Check <LinkCard title="Position encoding" href="/reference/position-encoding/" /> for the limits behind `None` results.


---

---
title: Registering source files
description: Register single files, loops, all-or-nothing batches and OS paths; control capacity and resolve duplicate registrations.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to choose the right registration API for your situation and to
predict how Sourcier resolves duplicates and capacity. Registration happens
in the build phase; finalization then sorts entries by path and assigns
stable one-based ids.

## Register a single file

`add_file` accepts any path that converts to `&str` and any content that
converts to `Vec<u8>`:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::SourceFilesMap;

let mut files = SourceFilesMap::<u8>::new();
files
    .add_file("src/main.rs", b"fn main() {}")
    .expect("capacity available");`} />

The only failure is an exhausted id type (`MapError::TooManyFiles`).

## Register in a loop

`add_file` consumes and returns the map or builder for chaining. Inside a
loop, prefer the mutating variant `add_file_mut`, which keeps the value in
place after an error:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{SourceFilesBuilder, SourceFilesMap};

fn collect(names: &[&str]) -> SourceFilesMap<u16> {
    let mut builder = SourceFilesBuilder::<u16>::with_capacity(names.len());
    for name in names {
        builder
            .add_file_mut(format!("src/{name}.rs"), format!("// {name}"))
            .expect("u16 capacity");
    }
    builder.finalize().expect("no capacity issue")
}`} />

`with_capacity` pre-reserves storage for the expected file count and reduces
reallocations while building.

## Register an all-or-nothing batch

`add_files` registers an iterator of `(path, content)` pairs and leaves the
map or builder exactly as it was when any pair fails:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::SourceFilesMap;

let mut files = SourceFilesMap::<u8>::new();
let batch = vec![
    ("a.rs", &b"fn a() {}"[..]),
    ("b.rs", &b"fn b() {}"[..]),
];

files.add_files(batch).expect("capacity available");
files.finalize().expect("no capacity issue");
assert_eq!(files.len(), 2);`} />

Because the batch is atomic, a failure partway through cannot leave a
partially registered set behind.

## Register OS paths

Tools that hold `Path`/`PathBuf` values register through `add_path`. Paths
are stored as `str`, so a path carrying bytes that are not valid UTF-8 fails
with `MapError::PathNotUtf8`, which carries the lossy rendering of the path
for diagnostics:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{MapError, SourceFilesBuilder};
use std::path::PathBuf;

let files = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::new()
    .add_path(PathBuf::from("src/main.rs"), b"fn main() {}")
    .expect("utf-8 path")
    .finalize()
    .expect("no capacity issue");

assert_eq!(files.get_id("src/main.rs"), Some(1));`} />

<Aside type="caution">
	Non-UTF-8 paths cannot be registered losslessly. Convert them at the
	boundary of your tool and report `MapError::PathNotUtf8` with its `path`
	field to the user.
</Aside>

## Handle duplicate paths

You can register the same path any number of times. Duplicates are resolved
during `finalize`: the first registration of a path wins, later ones are
dropped, and the resolution holds even at hundreds-of-duplicates scale
(property-tested):

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::SourceFilesMap;

let mut files = SourceFilesMap::<u8>::new();
files.add_file("a.rs", b"first").expect("capacity available");
files.add_file("a.rs", b"second").expect("capacity available");
files.finalize().expect("no capacity issue");

assert_eq!(files.get_content(1), Some(&b"first"[..]));`} />

## Watch the capacity of the id type

The id type bounds how many files the map can address. Ids are one-based, so
`0` is never assigned:

| Id type | Max files | File id bits | Choose when |
| ------- | --------- | ------------ | ----------- |
| `u8`    | 255       | 8            | Single-crate tools, tests, small codebases |
| `u16`   | 65,535    | 16           | Language servers, monorepos, indexers |

Call `remaining_capacity` on a builder to learn how many more files the id
type can address:

<Code lang="rust" code={`let mut builder = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::new();
assert_eq!(builder.remaining_capacity(), 255);`} />

Exceeding the limit fails with `MapError::TooManyFiles { max }`, both during
registration and during finalization.

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Working with positions" href="/guides/working-with-positions/" /> to pack spans against the files you registered.
- Read <LinkCard title="The two-phase lifecycle" href="/explanation/two-phase-lifecycle/" /> to understand why finalization is the phase boundary.
- Check <LinkCard title="Errors" href="/reference/errors/" /> when a registration call returns an error variant.


---

---
title: Tuning performance
description: Pre-reserve capacity, choose the right id type, opt into parallel index construction and trim features for faster builds and leaner binaries.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide when maps grow large, when finalization shows up in profiles,
or when binary size matters. The numbers quoted here come from the bundled
criterion suite (`cargo bench -p sourcier-core`) on the reference machine
comparing 2.0 against the 1.0 baseline; treat them as indicative.

## Pre-reserve capacity

Both the map and the builder accept an expected file count, which
pre-reserves storage and reduces reallocations while building:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::SourceFilesBuilder;

let builder = SourceFilesBuilder::<u16>::with_capacity(4_096);
assert_eq!(builder.remaining_capacity(), 65_535);`} />

## Choose the smallest id type that fits

The id type sets both the capacity and the packed encoding:

| Id type | Max files | File id bits | Best for |
| ------- | --------- | ------------ | -------- |
| `u8`    | 255       | 8            | Single-crate tools, tests, small codebases |
| `u16`   | 65,535    | 16           | Language servers, monorepos, indexers |

Smaller id types leave more bits to the other fields of the packed `u64`, and
`u8` positions are the `CompactAbsolutePosition` alias that many diagnostics
caches prefer.

## Opt into parallel index construction

Line-offset indexes are built with a single `memchr`-accelerated scan by
default. The opt-in `parallel` feature spreads that scan across cores with
`rayon` for huge file sets:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
sourcier = { version = "2.0", features = ["parallel"] }`} />

<Aside type="note">
	On a 2-core reference VM the thread-pool overhead outweighed the scan
	savings, which is why the feature is opt-in. Enable it on many-core build
	machines where file sets are large.
</Aside>

## Trim features for a leaner build

Default features pull in `serde`, `view` and `rt-feedback`. Disable what your
tool does not use:

<Code lang="toml" code={`[dependencies]
sourcier = { version = "2.0", default-features = false, features = ["view"] }`} />

Each trimmed feature removes code from the binary and work from the build;
see [Feature flags](/reference/feature-flags/) for what each one gates.

## Know what the costs are

Measured scenarios from the bundled benchmark suite:

| Scenario | 1.0 | 2.0 | Change |
| -------- | --- | --- | ------ |
| Finalize 100 files × 50 lines | ~64 us | ~41 us | **-35%** |
| Finalize 500 files × 100 lines | ~709 us | ~513 us | **-28%** |
| Finalize phase only, 2,000 × 200 lines | ~3.7 ms | ~2.8 ms | **-25%** |
| 1,000 multi-line `view` extractions | ~14.4 us | ~4.4 us | **-70%** |
| Line offsets for 100 files × 1,000 lines | ~0.79 ms | ~0.69 ms | **-12%** |
| 1,000 offset-to-(line, col) probes | — | ~8.2 us | new |
| Single-line `view_str` span | — | ~257 ns | new |
| 2,000 path-to-id lookups (hits) | ~34 us | ~41 us | see note |
| 2,000 path-to-id lookups (misses) | — | ~33 us | new |

The 2.0 path-to-id index trades a small amount of hit latency (~20%) for
byte-exact verification, HashDoS-resistant per-map seeding, zero allocations
at finalization and roughly half the lookup-state memory. Hits and misses
both terminate on the first empty slot, so misses are as cheap as hits. The
design rationale lives in [Performance design](/explanation/performance-design/).

## Pin the costs in CI

The benchmark tracks for the builder, the offset bridge and lookups are part
of the repository, so you can pin the costs your tool depends on:

<Code lang="bash" code={`cargo bench -p sourcier-core`} />

## Next steps

- Read <LinkCard title="Performance design" href="/explanation/performance-design/" /> for the data-structure rationale behind the numbers.
- Follow <LinkCard title="Registering source files" href="/guides/registering-files/" /> for the capacity APIs used above.
- Check <LinkCard title="Feature flags" href="/reference/feature-flags/" /> before trimming further.


---

---
title: Sharing usage statistics
description: Observe finalization activity across maps and threads with the lock-free RuntimeFeedback context.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to collect usage statistics when your tool builds many source
file maps. Everything on this page requires the default `rt-feedback`
feature. The context is lock-free: finalizing a map updates the counters
with atomic operations, so multiple maps and threads can report into the same
context without blocking.

## Create a shared feedback context

Create one `RuntimeFeedback`, wrap it in an `Arc` and hand it to the map:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;

use sourcier::{RuntimeFeedback, SourceFilesMap};

let feedback = Arc::new(RuntimeFeedback::new());

let mut files = SourceFilesMap::<u8>::with_feedback(Arc::clone(&feedback));
files.add_file("a.rs", b"fn a() {}").expect("capacity available");
files.finalize().expect("no capacity issue");`} />

Builders accept the same context through
`SourceFilesBuilder::with_feedback`.

## Read a snapshot

`snapshot` returns an immutable, `Copy` snapshot of the counters:

<Code lang="rust" code={`let snapshot = feedback.snapshot();

assert_eq!(snapshot.total_files, 1);
assert_eq!(snapshot.total_bytes, 9);
assert_eq!(snapshot.max_file_size, 9);
assert_eq!(snapshot.usage_count, 1);`} />

The snapshot fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `total_files` | Number of files registered by the last finalized map |
| `total_bytes` | Total content bytes registered by the last finalized map |
| `max_file_size` | Size in bytes of the largest file of the last finalized map |
| `usage_count` | Number of finalizations that reported into this context |

<Aside type="note">
	Each successful finalization **overwrites** the per-map totals (`total_files`,
	`total_bytes`, `max_file_size`) with that map's values and **increments**
	`usage_count`. Totals therefore describe the most recent finalization, not
	the sum of all finalizations.
</Aside>

## Report from multiple threads

The reporting path takes no locks, so threads only contend on atomic
instructions. Share the `Arc` across workers and read the counters whenever
you need them:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use std::sync::Arc;

use sourcier::{RuntimeFeedback, SourceFilesBuilder};

let feedback = Arc::new(RuntimeFeedback::new());

let handles: Vec<_> = (0..4)
    .map(|i| {
        let feedback = Arc::clone(&feedback);
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut files = SourceFilesBuilder::<u8>::with_feedback(feedback);
            files
                .add_file(format!("{i}.rs"), b"fn x() {}")
                .expect("capacity available");
            files.finalize().expect("no capacity issue");
        })
    })
    .collect();

for handle in handles {
    handle.join().expect("worker finished");
}

assert_eq!(feedback.snapshot().usage_count, 4);`} />

With the default `serde` feature, `FeedbackSnapshot` also implements
`Serialize` and `Deserialize`, so you can log or persist snapshots directly.

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Registering source files" href="/guides/registering-files/" /> for the registration API the counters observe.
- Check <LinkCard title="API surface" href="/reference/api/" /> for the full `RuntimeFeedback` and `FeedbackSnapshot` signatures.


---

---
title: Working with positions
description: Create packed spans with checked and unchecked constructors, convert between absolute and relative forms, and order or serialize them.
type: how-to
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide to create, validate, convert, order and serialize packed
positions. Two types cover the two situations you meet in a tool:
`AbsolutePosition<Id>` addresses a span in a specific file of a map, and
`RelativePosition` carries only the span — start line, start column, end
line, end column — so you can store or compare it without binding it to a
file.

## Create an absolute position

`AbsolutePosition::new` packs the five components as-is. It is infallible and
zero-cost:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::AbsolutePosition;

// file id 7, start 2:5, end 2:22 (inclusive).
let pos = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(7, 2, 5, 2, 22);`} />

Lines and columns are one-based; the end line and end column are inclusive.
The packed value orders like a natural lexicographic ordering of spans, so
positions sort with integer comparison.

## Validate spans with checked constructors

When a span comes from user input or an untrusted source, use `try_new`. It
returns `PositionError::InvalidRange` when any line or column is zero, or
when the start does not come before (or exactly at) the end:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::AbsolutePosition;

assert!(AbsolutePosition::<u8>::try_new(1, 2, 1, 1, 1).is_err());
assert!(AbsolutePosition::<u8>::try_new(1, 1, 5, 1, 4).is_err());
assert!(AbsolutePosition::<u8>::try_new(1, 1, 1, 1, 1).is_ok());
assert!(AbsolutePosition::<u8>::try_new(1, 1, 4, 1, 5).is_ok());`} />

`RelativePosition::try_new` applies the same rules to file-agnostic spans.

## Convert between absolute and relative

Strip the file id with `to_relative`, and attach one with
`RelativePosition::to_absolute`:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{AbsolutePosition, RelativePosition};

let abs = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(7, 2, 5, 2, 22);
assert_eq!(abs.to_relative(), RelativePosition::new(2, 5, 2, 22));

let rel = RelativePosition::new(2, 5, 2, 22);
assert_eq!(rel.to_absolute(3_u8), AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(3, 2, 5, 2, 22));`} />

`From<AbsolutePosition<Id>> for RelativePosition` is also implemented, so
`let rel: RelativePosition = abs.into();` works.

## Build spans in const contexts

`RelativePosition::new` and `RelativePosition::from_raw` are `const fn`, so
spans can be built and stored in `const` and `static` items:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::RelativePosition;

const STD_SPAN: RelativePosition = RelativePosition::new(1, 1, 1, 1);`} />

<Aside type="note">
	`AbsolutePosition::new` is not a `const fn` because it routes the id
	through the `FileId` trait; use the const `RelativePosition` constructors
	when you need compile-time packing.
</Aside>

## Round-trip through the raw encoding

`as_raw` returns the stable `u64` encoding and `from_raw` rebuilds a
position from it. For absolute positions, `from_raw` returns `None` when the
embedded file id cannot be represented by `Id` — including the
never-assigned id `0`:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::AbsolutePosition;

let pos = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(42, 1, 2, 3, 4);
let copy = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::from_raw(pos.as_raw()).expect("valid raw value");
assert_eq!(pos, copy);`} />

The bit layout is stable across semver-compatible releases, so raw values
can be persisted safely. See [Position encoding](/reference/position-encoding/)
for the exact bit ranges.

## Order and compare

Positions derive `PartialOrd` and `Ord`. Ordering by the packed value equals
ordering spans lexicographically: file id first, then start line, start
column, end line and end column:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::AbsolutePosition;

let a = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(1, 1, 1, 1, 1);
let b = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(1, 1, 1, 1, 2);
let c = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(1, 2, 1, 2, 1);
let d = AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(2, 1, 1, 1, 1);
assert!(a < b && b < c && c < d);`} />

## Serialize positions

With the default `serde` feature, both position types implement
`Serialize` and `Deserialize`, and a round trip preserves the bits exactly:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::RelativePosition;

let pos = RelativePosition::new(2, 5, 3, 10);
let json = serde_json::to_string(&pos).expect("serializable");
assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<RelativePosition>(&json).expect("valid"), pos);`} />

## Render spans as text

`Display` renders `start_line:start_column-end_line:end_column`:

<Code lang="rust" code={`use sourcier::{AbsolutePosition, RelativePosition};

assert_eq!(AbsolutePosition::<u8>::new(1, 10, 5, 12, 20).to_string(), "10:5-12:20");
assert_eq!(RelativePosition::new(2, 5, 2, 22).to_string(), "2:5-2:22");`} />

To render a position together with its file path as `path:line:column`, use
`display_position` on a finalized map — see
[Views and navigation](/guides/navigating-source/).

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Views and navigation" href="/guides/navigating-source/" /> to bridge byte offsets and positions.
- Check <LinkCard title="Position encoding" href="/reference/position-encoding/" /> before persisting raw values.
- Check <LinkCard title="Errors" href="/reference/errors/" /> for the exact shape of `PositionError::InvalidRange`.

title: Sourcier
description: Compact and efficient source file mapping and position tracking for Rust — register files once, pack every span into a single u64.
template: splash
type: explanation
hero:
  title: "Sourcier"

  image:

      link: /reference/api/
      icon: external
---

import { Card, CardGrid, LinkButton, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Sourcier is built for diagnostics-heavy tools — compilers, linters, formatters,
language servers and code editors — that need positions which are cheap to
build, compare, store and serialize, yet still resolve back to the exact bytes
of the file they point at. Instead of dragging `String` paths and four `usize`
fields through every diagnostic, you pack the whole span into one `u64` and
keep the heavy data in a single immutable registry.

## Choose your path

<CardGrid stagger>
	<Card title="Learn the golden path">
		Follow the tutorial to register files, finalize a map, and extract the
		exact bytes of a span in about ten minutes.
		<LinkCard title="Your first source map" href="/tutorials/getting-started/" />
	</Card>
	<Card title="Solve a specific task">
		Task-oriented guides cover installation, registration, packed positions,
		byte views, shared statistics, errors and performance tuning.
		<LinkCard title="Browse the how-to guides" href="/guides/installation/" />
	</Card>
	<Card title="Look something up">
		Reference pages document the full API surface, the stable `u64` bit
		layouts, feature flags and every error variant.
		<LinkCard title="Open the reference" href="/reference/api/" />
	</Card>
	<Card title="Understand the design">
		Explanation pages walk through the two-phase lifecycle, the verified
		path index and the safety guarantees that shape the API.
		<LinkCard title="Read the design notes" href="/explanation/why-sourcier/" />
	</Card>
</CardGrid>

<LinkButton href="/tutorials/getting-started/" icon="right-arrow">Start the tutorial</LinkButton>

## Highlights

- **One `u64` per span.** File id, start line, start column, end line and end
  column are bit-packed together. Positions are `Copy`, cache-friendly, order
  naturally as integers and survive serialization round trips bit-exactly.
- **Constant-time lookups.** After finalization, path to id, id to path and id
  to content are all O(1); line and column navigation is O(log n).
- **Byte-accurate views.** With the default `view` feature, a position resolves
  to the exact bytes it covers, including multi-line spans and line terminators.
- **No unsafe code.** The whole workspace is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, error
  enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, and the `FileId` trait is sealed.


---

---
title: API surface
description: Complete reference for every public type, trait and function Sourcier exports, with signatures, parameters and return values.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Badge, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Sourcier is a facade crate: `sourcier` re-exports the full API of
`sourcier-core`, so `sourcier::...` is the only path you ever need. This page
lists every public item with its signature. The rustdoc-generated reference
lives on [docs.rs/sourcier](https://docs.rs/sourcier).

## Registry types

### `SourceFilesMap<Id: FileId>`

Two-phase registry: register files, finalize, then query immutably.

| Method | Signature | Returns | Description |
| ------ | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `new` | `pub fn new() -> Self` | `Self` | Empty map without pre-reserved storage |
| `with_capacity` | `pub fn with_capacity(expected_files: usize) -> Self` | `Self` | Empty map that pre-reserves storage |
| `with_feedback` <Badge text="rt-feedback" size="small" /> | `pub fn with_feedback(feedback: Arc<RuntimeFeedback>) -> Self` | `Self` | Map that reports finalization statistics |
| `add_file` | `pub fn add_file(&mut self, path: impl AsRef<str>, content: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | Registers one file |
| `add_files` | `pub fn add_files<I, P, C>(&mut self, files: I) -> Result<(), MapError> where I: IntoIterator<Item = (P, C)>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | All-or-nothing batch registration |
| `add_path` | `pub fn add_path(&mut self, path: impl AsRef<Path>, content: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | Registers an OS path; fails with `PathNotUtf8` on non-UTF-8 paths |
| `finalize` | `pub fn finalize(&mut self) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | Sorts by path, deduplicates, assigns one-based ids |
| `is_finalized` | `pub fn is_finalized(&self) -> bool` | `bool` | Phase query |
| `len` / `is_empty` | `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` / `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` | — | Entry count |
| `total_bytes` | `pub fn total_bytes(&self) -> usize` | `usize` | Total registered content bytes |
| `paths` | `pub fn paths(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str>` | iterator | Registered paths |
| `iter` | `pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, Id>` | `Iter<'_, Id>` | Files with ids; yields nothing before finalization |
| `get_id` | `pub fn get_id(&self, path: &str) -> Option<Id>` | `Option<Id>` | Path to id, O(1) after finalization |
| `get_path` | `pub fn get_path(&self, id: Id) -> Option<&str>` | `Option<&str>` | Id to path, O(1) |
| `get_content` | `pub fn get_content(&self, id: Id) -> Option<&[u8]>` | `Option<&[u8]>` | Id to content bytes, O(1) |
| `get` | `pub fn get(&self, id: Id) -> Option<FileRef<'_, Id>>` | `Option<FileRef<'_, Id>>` | Id to a borrowed `FileRef { id, path, content }` |
| `view` <Badge text="view" size="small" /> | `pub fn view(&self, id: Id, pos: &impl SourceFilePosition) -> Option<&[u8]>` | `Option<&[u8]>` | Exact bytes the position covers |
| `view_str` <Badge text="view" size="small" /> | `pub fn view_str(&self, id: Id, pos: &impl SourceFilePosition) -> Option<&str>` | `Option<&str>` | UTF-8 view; `None` on non-UTF-8 boundaries |
| `line_offsets` <Badge text="view" size="small" /> | `pub fn line_offsets(&self, id: Id) -> Option<&LineOffsets>` | `Option<&LineOffsets>` | Per-file line index |
| `position_from_offset` <Badge text="view" size="small" /> | `pub fn position_from_offset(&self, id: Id, offset: usize) -> Option<AbsolutePosition<Id>>` | `Option<AbsolutePosition<Id>>` | Byte offset to point position, O(log n) |
| `offset_from_position` <Badge text="view" size="small" /> | `pub fn offset_from_position(&self, id: Id, pos: &impl SourceFilePosition) -> Option<usize>` | `Option<usize>` | Span start to byte offset, O(log n) |
| `display_position` | `pub fn display_position(&self, id: Id, pos: &impl SourceFilePosition) -> Option<PositionDisplay<'_>>` | `Option<PositionDisplay<'_>>` | Zero-allocation `path:line:column` renderer |

`&SourceFilesMap` implements `IntoIterator`, yielding `FileRef` entries in id
order; use it like `for entry in &files { ... }`.

### `SourceFilesBuilder<Id: FileId>`

Type-state build-phase companion of `SourceFilesMap`. It only exposes
registration, so `MapError::Finalized` and `MapError::AlreadyFinalized` are
unrepresentable, and `finalize` consumes the builder and hands back the
lookup-ready map.

| Method | Signature | Returns | Description |
| ------ | --------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `new` | `pub fn new() -> Self` | `Self` | Empty builder |
| `with_capacity` | `pub fn with_capacity(expected_files: usize) -> Self` | `Self` | Builder that pre-reserves storage |
| `with_feedback` <Badge text="rt-feedback" size="small" /> | `pub fn with_feedback(feedback: Arc<RuntimeFeedback>) -> Self` | `Self` | Builder that reports finalization statistics |
| `add_file` | `pub fn add_file(self, path: impl AsRef<str>, content: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<Self, MapError>` | `Result<Self, MapError>` | Chainable registration |
| `add_file_mut` | `pub fn add_file_mut(&mut self, path: impl AsRef<str>, content: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | Registration for loops |
| `add_files` | `pub fn add_files<I, P, C>(&mut self, files: I) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | All-or-nothing batch |
| `add_path` | `pub fn add_path(&mut self, path: impl AsRef<Path>, content: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), MapError>` | `Result<(), MapError>` | OS-path registration |
| `len` / `is_empty` | `pub fn len(&self) -> usize` / `pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool` | — | Files registered so far |
| `paths` | `pub fn paths(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str>` | iterator | Registered paths, in registration order |
| `finalize` | `pub fn finalize(self) -> Result<SourceFilesMap<Id>, MapError>` | `Result<SourceFilesMap<Id>, MapError>` | Consumes the builder, returns the map |
| `remaining_capacity` | `pub fn remaining_capacity(&self) -> usize` | `usize` | How many more files the id type can address |

## Position types

### `AbsolutePosition<Id: FileId>`

A span inside a specific source file, packed into a single `u64`. Aliases:
`CompactAbsolutePosition = AbsolutePosition<u8>`,
`StandardAbsolutePosition = AbsolutePosition<u16>`.

| Item | Signature | Description |
| ---- | --------- | ----------- |
| `new` | `pub fn new(file_id: Id, start_line: u16, start_col: u8, end_line: u16, end_col: u8) -> Self` | Infallible, zero-cost packing; no validation |
| `try_new` | `pub fn try_new(...) -> Result<Self, PositionError>` | Same packing with range validation |
| `from_raw` | `pub fn from_raw(raw: u64) -> Option<Self>` | Rebuilds from the raw encoding; `None` for unrepresentable ids (including `0`) |
| `as_raw` | `pub const fn as_raw(&self) -> u64` | Stable raw encoding |
| `to_relative` | `pub fn to_relative(self) -> RelativePosition` | Strips the file id |
| `file_id` | `pub fn file_id(&self) -> Id` | File id component |
| `Display` | `"{start_line}:{start_col}-{end_line}:{end_col}"` | `"2:5-2:22"` |
| Derives | `Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash` + `serde` with the default feature | Ordering matches lexicographic span order |

### `RelativePosition`

A file-agnostic span packed into the low 48 bits of a `u64`; the high 16 bits
are always zero.

| Item | Signature | Description |
| ---- | --------- | ----------- |
| `new` | `pub const fn new(start_line: u16, start_col: u8, end_line: u16, end_col: u8) -> Self` | Const packing for `const`/`static` items |
| `try_new` | `pub fn try_new(...) -> Result<Self, PositionError>` | Validated packing |
| `from_raw` | `pub const fn from_raw(raw: u64) -> Self` | Const rebuild; masks the high 16 bits |
| `as_raw` | `pub const fn as_raw(&self) -> u64` | Raw encoding |
| `to_absolute` | `pub fn to_absolute<Id: FileId>(self, file_id: Id) -> AbsolutePosition<Id>` | Attaches a file id |
| `Display` | `"{start_line}:{start_col}-{end_line}:{end_col}"` | `"2:5-3:10"` |

### `SourceFilePosition` (trait)

Uniform accessor trait over both position kinds, implemented by
`AbsolutePosition<Id>` and `RelativePosition`. Write generic helpers against
it:

| Method | Signature | Returns |
| ------ | --------- | ------- |
| `source_file_id` | `fn source_file_id(&self) -> Option<u16>` | `None` for relative positions |
| `start_line` | `fn start_line(&self) -> u16` | One-based start line |
| `start_column` | `fn start_column(&self) -> u8` | One-based start column |
| `end_line` | `fn end_line(&self) -> u16` | One-based end line |
| `end_column` | `fn end_column(&self) -> u8` | One-based end column |

## Id type

### `FileId` (sealed trait)

Implemented only by `u8` and `u16`; sealed, so new methods can be added
without breaking downstream code. Associated constants: `MAX_FILES`,
`FILE_ID_BITS`, `FILE_ID_SHIFT`, `START_LINE_SHIFT`, `START_COL_SHIFT`,
`END_LINE_SHIFT`, `END_COL_SHIFT`, `FILE_ID_MASK`, `LINE_MASK`, `COL_MASK`.

| Method | Signature | Description |
| ------ | --------- | ----------- |
| `from_index` | `fn from_index(index: usize) -> Option<Self>` | `index 0 -> id 1`; `None` out of range |
| `to_raw` | `fn to_raw(self) -> u64` | Raw numeric value |

## View feature types

### `LineOffsets`

Compact per-line byte offset index, 4 bytes per line, files up to 4 GiB.

| Method | Signature | Description |
| ------ | --------- | ----------- |
| `compute` | `pub fn compute(content: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, MapError>` | Builds the index with a single `memchr` scan; `FileTooLarge` beyond 4 GiB |
| `line_count` | `pub fn line_count(&self) -> usize` | Number of lines |
| `content_length` | `pub fn content_length(&self) -> usize` | Total byte length |
| `line_starts` | `pub fn line_starts(&self) -> &[u32]` | The raw `u32` offset list |
| `line_range` | `pub fn line_range(&self, line: usize) -> Option<Range<usize>>` | One-based line to byte range; line `0` resolves to `None` |
| `line_col_from_offset` | `pub fn line_col_from_offset(&self, offset: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)>` | Offset to one-based `(line, column)` |
| `offset_from_line_col` | `pub fn offset_from_line_col(&self, line: usize, col: usize) -> Option<usize>` | Inverse mapping |

## Runtime statistics types

### `RuntimeFeedback` :badge[rt-feedback]

Lock-free usage statistics shared between maps via `Arc`.

| Method | Signature | Description |
| ------ | --------- | ----------- |
| `new` | `pub fn new() -> Self` | Empty context |
| `snapshot` | `pub fn snapshot(&self) -> FeedbackSnapshot` | Immutable counter snapshot |

### `FeedbackSnapshot` :badge[rt-feedback]

`Copy` snapshot with public fields `total_files: usize`, `total_bytes: u64`,
`max_file_size: usize`, `usage_count: u64`. Totals describe the most recent
finalization; `usage_count` accumulates.

### `PositionDisplay<'a>`

Zero-allocation `path:line:column` renderer created by
`display_position`. Implements `Display`; the string is formatted lazily from
borrowed data.

## Iterator types

`Iter<'a, Id>` — created by `iter` and by `&SourceFilesMap`'s
`IntoIterator`. Yields `FileRef<'a, Id> { id: Id, path: &'a str, content:
&'a [u8] }` and yields nothing before finalization, because ids only exist
afterwards.

## Error types

`MapError` and `PositionError` are `#[non_exhaustive]` enums; see
[Errors](/reference/errors/) for every variant with its fields.

<Aside type="note">
        Signatures are abbreviated on this page: trait bounds such as
        `Id: FileId` are implied, and long parameter lists are elided with `...`
        only where the reference table above lists them in full.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- Check <LinkCard title="Position encoding" href="/reference/position-encoding/" /> for the bit layouts behind `as_raw`.
- Check <LinkCard title="Feature flags" href="/reference/feature-flags/" /> for what each badge on this page means.
- Browse [docs.rs/sourcier](https://docs.rs/sourcier) for the rustdoc-generated API.

---
title: Changelog
description: Release history of Sourcier, currently version 2.0 with the builder, offset bridge and verified path index.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This page summarizes the release history. The canonical, generated changelog
lives in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/elcoosp/sourcier/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
and is produced with git-cliff from the commit history.

## 2.0 (current)

The 2.0 release line focuses on the developer experience around the core
engine and on a leaner, safer lookup path.

### Added

- The type-state `SourceFilesBuilder`: chaining registration with
  compile-time phase separation, `add_file_mut` for loops, and
  `remaining_capacity`.
- All-or-nothing batch registration with `add_files`.
- OS-path registration with `add_path` and a dedicated
  `MapError::PathNotUtf8` for non-UTF-8 paths.
- The offset bridge: `position_from_offset` and `offset_from_position`
  convert between byte offsets and packed positions in O(log n) with no
  allocation.
- `PositionDisplay` and `display_position` render `path:line:column`
  diagnostics without allocating.
- Const constructors and span conversions for positions
  (`RelativePosition::new` and `from_raw` are `const fn`).
- A verified open-addressed path index with inline path storage (paths up to
  30 bytes live inside their entry, with no heap allocation).
- Exposed line starts accessor and optimized vector initialization in the
  core engine.

### Changed

- Removed the obsolete `clo`, `fid` and `sfm` modules and restructured the
  core modules.
- Enriched crate-level documentation with memory-footprint metrics.
- The `parallel` feature is forwarded from the facade to the core library.

### Performance

- Finalization improved by 25-35% across benchmark scenarios.
- Multi-line `view` extractions improved by 70%.
- The path-to-id index trades ~20% hit latency for byte-exact verification,
  HashDoS-resistant per-map seeding, zero allocations at finalization and
  roughly half the lookup-state memory.

### Compatibility

- The 2.0 wire format of `SourceFilesMap` dropped the redundant
  `path_to_id` table; it is derived from the sorted entries and rebuilt on
  load.
- 1.0 payloads that still carry the field deserialize without error and are
  ignored.

## 0.1.0 (2025-12-19)

First public release:

- `fid`, `sfm` and `sfp` modules for compact `u64` position representation
  and O(1) path-to-id mapping.
- `SourceFilesMap` with content storage and `get_content`.
- `RuntimeFeedback` proof of concept with `with_feedback`.
- The `view` feature and optional `serde` support.

<Aside type="note">
        In the repository, the 2.0.0 section currently sits under the Unreleased
        heading of the generated changelog; the workspace version in Cargo.toml
        is 2.0.0.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- Read the full [changelog on GitHub](https://github.com/elcoosp/sourcier/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
- Check <LinkCard title="The two-phase lifecycle" href="/explanation/two-phase-lifecycle/" /> for the design the 2.0 builder formalizes.

---
title: Errors
description: Every MapError and PositionError variant with fields, display strings and the conditions that produce them.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Both error enums derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq` and `Eq`, implement
`std::error::Error` through `thiserror`, and are `#[non_exhaustive]`: match
arms outside this crate always contain a catch-all arm.

## `MapError`

Errors produced while building or querying a
`SourceFilesMap`.

| Variant | Fields | Display string | Produced by |
| ------- | ------ | -------------- | ----------- |
| `TooManyFiles` | `max: usize` | `cannot register more than {max} files for this file id type` | `add_file`, `add_files`, `add_path`, `finalize` beyond id capacity (255 for `u8`, 65,535 for `u16`) |
| `AlreadyFinalized` | — | `the source files map has already been finalized` | `finalize` called twice on a raw map |
| `Finalized` | — | `cannot modify the source files map after finalization` | `add_file`, `add_files` or `add_path` after finalization |
| `FileTooLarge` | `size: u64` | `file content of {size} bytes exceeds the 4 GiB line offset limit` | Line-offset construction for a file above `u32::MAX` bytes |
| `PathNotUtf8` | `path: String` | `path is not valid UTF-8: {path}` | `add_path` with a path that is not valid UTF-8; the field carries the lossy rendering (invalid bytes replaced by `U+FFFD`) |

<Aside type="note">
	`Finalized` and `AlreadyFinalized` are unrepresentable through
	`SourceFilesBuilder`: the type-state builder only exposes registration,
	and `finalize` consumes it. They remain reachable through the raw map.
</Aside>

## `PositionError`

Errors produced by the checked `try_new` constructors of `AbsolutePosition`
and `RelativePosition`.

| Variant | Fields | Display string |
| ------- | ------ | -------------- |
| `InvalidRange` | `start_line: u16`, `start_col: u8`, `end_line: u16`, `end_col: u8` | `invalid position range: start {start_line}:{start_col} must not come after end {end_line}:{end_col} and all lines and columns must be at least 1` |

`InvalidRange` fires when any of the following fails:

- `start_line >= 1` and `end_line >= 1`
- `start_col >= 1` and `end_col >= 1`
- `start_line < end_line`, or `start_line == end_line && start_col <= end_col`

## Results by API

| API | Success | Failure |
| --- | ------- | ------- |
| `add_file` / `add_file_mut` | Registers the file | `TooManyFiles` |
| `add_files` | Registers every file, all-or-nothing | `TooManyFiles`; the map is unchanged on failure |
| `add_path` | Registers the file | `PathNotUtf8`, `TooManyFiles` |
| `finalize` | Assigns ids, switches phase | `AlreadyFinalized`, `TooManyFiles` |
| `LineOffsets::compute` | Builds the index | `FileTooLarge` |
| `AbsolutePosition::try_new` / `RelativePosition::try_new` | Packs the span | `InvalidRange` |
| `get_id`, `get_path`, `get_content`, `get`, `view`, `view_str`, `position_from_offset`, `offset_from_position`, `display_position` | `Option` results | No errors — unknown ids, unfinalized maps and unresolvable spans return `None` |

## Next steps

- Follow <LinkCard title="Handling errors" href="/guides/handling-errors/" /> for recovery patterns per variant.
- Check <LinkCard title="Position encoding" href="/reference/position-encoding/" /> for the limits behind `FileTooLarge` and `TooManyFiles`.
